summary.one_liner: LibreSpeed is a lightweight, self-hostable browser-based internet speed test written in JavaScript that measures download, upload, ping and jitter without Flash or Java.
summary.what_it_does: The front end is JavaScript using XMLHttpRequest and Web Workers, so tests run in the browser with no plugins. It measures download speed, upload speed, ping and jitter, and can show the client's IP address, ISP and distance to the server. The README describes optional telemetry, results sharing, and multiple points of test. A separate stability test page (stability.html) repeatedly measures ping over a chosen duration, reports average, min, max, jitter and failed-request percentages, draws a live latency chart, supports threshold alerts, and exports CSV. The server side is provided in PHP with MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite or Microsoft SQL Server options for storing results; the README also points to separate Go, Rust and Node.js backends and Android, CLI and .NET clients. A Docker image is available, and the README includes a classic and a modern UI selected via config.json.
use_cases: self-host a internet speed test for a network or office
measure download and upload speed from a browser
check ping and jitter to a local server
monitor connection latency stability over time
run multi-location speed tests with several servers
deploy a speed test page in Docker
how_to_run: Download the source code and extract it
Copy the project files to your web server's shared folder (e.g. /var/www/html/speedtest for Apache), keeping the layout as in the repository, including the frontend/ directory
Optionally copy the results folder and set up the database using its config file
Ensure file permissions allow read and execute access where needed
Alternatively, use the Docker image (README recommends the latest tag; see Docker documentation for details)
stack: MariaDB / MySQL / PostgreSQL / SQLite / Microsoft SQL Server
notable: No Flash, Java or WebSocket dependency; runs in the browser with XMLHttpRequest and Web Workers
Stability test page with live latency chart, loss tracking, threshold alerts and CSV export
Multiple backend implementations (PHP, Go, Rust, partial Node.js) and clients (Android, CLI, .NET)
Classic and modern UI with a design switcher driven by config.json
Weekly Docker image rebuilds to refresh the ipinfo database used for ISP detection
caveats: Node.js backend is partial and the README says it is not recommended at the moment
Requires a web server with PHP (or another backend) and a fast internet connection to get meaningful results
Database storage for results is optional; setup involves configuring a database
